belief: Why try? I can never succeed.
origins: Repeated failure at school, work, or tasks teaches that effort leads nowhere. Learned helplessness protects us from disappointment but also from growth.
teaches: “I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength.” “The LORD is my strength and my song, and He has become my salvation.” “Whatever you do, work at it with your whole being, for the Lord and not for men” (Colossians 3:23). Success is not only measured by grades or speed. Each honest effort, each step forward, matters to God. Choose small, achievable goals and celebrate them.
self_statements: I was not made for this.
It is safer not to try.
errors: Believing I either succeed fully or fail.
Feeling defeated and concluding it is pointless.
questions: When have I succeeded, even in something small?
What would a tiny, achievable goal look like?
What does Scripture say about strength?
How can I define success differently?
truth: Success includes honest effort and small steps. With Christ’s strength and the right help, I can try again and grow, and God honors faithfulness.
hw_truths: I can do all things through Christ.
log: Each week, note one small win.
actions: Ask a tutor, coach, or friend.
prayer: Lord, I am tired of failing. Give me strength for small steps, patient helpers, and joy in honest effort. Amen.
